Lex Plataformae · What did the platform take from you?
<1><2>What did the platform take from you?</2></1><3><4>Why doesn't a digital purchase end at delivery?</4></3><5><6>When did this start to seem normal?</6></5>

It was not your carelessness. The same company that sells the access writes the rules, applies the punishments, keeps the evidence and can change everything after the purchase. Start with what happened to you.
The vulnerability does not stem from private naivety, but from the absence of robust communicational demarcation between what was admitted, tolerated, official or forbidden.<1>p. 612</1>

[...] the Lex Plataformae designates a type of private ordering centred on a platform as an institutional core that defines rules, visibilities, sanctions and regimes of proof through continuous architecture and updating<1>p. 27</1>

When what is sold is a position of use sustained by a platform, the consumer relationship continues after payment. The supplier keeps governing the object, and it is this continuous governance that calls for its own criteria of duty, proof and consequence.

What is claimed is that, whenever the utility consumed presents itself as a position of enjoyment sustained by continuous private governance, there will be an intangible product in the legally relevant sense for the application of art. 3, § 1, of the CDC<1><2>1</2></1>.<3>p. 718</3>

The question comes from the introduction and organises the whole research. From here you reach the object, the instruments, the method that makes each inference checkable and the full text, with each sentence of the site linked to the page it came from.

Here are gathered the elements needed to make the investigation auditable, including the research strategy, the empirical scope and the techniques for collecting and reading the material used.<1>p. 47</1>
How the loss happens
You paid
You paid with money, with time or with attention, in a store, an app, a social network, an assistant or a game. What you received stayed inside an environment the company maintains.
<1>Passage already quoted above</1><2>p. 719</2>
The company kept control
The sale ended, but the company's power continued. It keeps writing the rules, updating the service and deciding what you see, what you can use and who stays.
<1>Passage already quoted above</1><2>p. 27</2>
It changed, punished or switched off
One day the function gets worse, reach drops, the account is suspended or the service ends. Often the decision arrives without a reason you can check or challenge.
The change of rule, the lowering of reach or the suspension do not even become a verifiable and disputable object within the system itself.<1>p. 381</1>
The loss stayed with you
The loss stays with you, and the records stay with whoever decided. But a digital service can change, just not in any way at all, and when it crosses the line someone answers for it.
